THE NOT-IN-COMBAT CAP closes it in BOTH bodies: v_combat_end := case when active_kind is distinct from 'combat' then least(now(), coalesce(active_since, 'epoch')) else now() end, and every window this pair prices now ENDS there instead of at now() - the bounty-free anchor window, the bounty accepted_at window and the combat-XP watermark window. It is an END-CAP, not a start-floor, and deliberately: a recovery line says 'nothing BEFORE this instant is payable' so it floors the START, while leaving combat says 'nothing AFTER it is', so a final post-fight flush (which is entirely pre-switch) still pays in full, a window straddling the switch pays only its pre-switch part, and a window entirely after the switch is <= 0 and credits ZERO with reason:'not_in_combat' from a short-circuit sited before every write. active_since IS the switch instant because set-activity.js sends restart:true on every transition and hr_apply stamps active_since = now() on that flag; coalesce(.., 'epoch') FAILS CLOSED on a missing active_since, which is the house rule (accrual.js SKIP.NO_ACTIVE_SINCE); least(.., now()) means a future active_since can only ever SHORTEN the window, so like the recovery floor this arm cannot become a faucet. The kind_mismatch journal field is KEPT (it now marks a call that was CAPPED rather than one that was paid) and each arm files at most ONE value-free ledger row per character per UTC day: kill_credit_not_in_combat / xp_credit_not_in_combat. THE WATERMARK, for this arm: the zero path returns before every write and stamps NOTHING, and that cannot let a later session re-claim pre-switch time twice, because the zero path only fires when v_elapsed <= 0, i.e. the watermark/anchor ALREADY covers the switch - and independently, re-entering combat runs set_activity (collectsFirst: true) which drives accrued_to = now(), so Condition 2's pre-existing greatest(v_wm, v_accrued) floors the next window at the moment the fight started. A window that STRADDLES the switch does not take the zero path: it pays its pre-switch part and stamps now() exactly as before, retiring the non-combat tail, which is correct. Sec 0 also gained a HALF-STATE guard: a body carrying the recovery marker but NOT the not-in-combat marker was patched by an earlier revision of this file and its anchors have moved, so the migration RAISES with recovery instructions rather than half-patching.
